Etomidate, as an anesthetic agent, is included in the broader category of general anesthetics, which in turn includes Desflurane. This pathway indicates that Etomidate may interact with Gabrb2 via Desflurane, though the direct binding affinity between Etomidate and Gabrb2 remains unquantified. The presence of a lowest common ancestor at the level of Anesthetic Agent and Heteroorganic Entity implies a biochemical pathway involving anesthetic agents and their interaction with receptor proteins. The evidence supports a possible role for Etomidate in modulating Gabrb2 activity, though further experimental validation is required to confirm the specific mechanism and binding affinity.
